title: Nonuniform Iterative Phasing Framework and Sampling Requirements for 3D Dynamical Inversion from Coherent Surface Scattering Imaging
summary: Coherent surface scattering imaging (CSSI) is an emerging experimental technique uniquely suited to probing the structure of thin nanostructures. In these experiments, a specimen is placed on a substrate, and a series of X-ray diffraction patterns is collected at grazing incidence angles as the specimen is rotated. However, reconstructing the specimen's 3D structure from the data is challenging due to dynamical scattering effects induced by the experimental geometry and the lack of direct phase measurements.
